chapter: Boston roadhouses and the Army band
title: Touring France, Paris dances and men in the band
summary: The band plays for officers across Europe, Vodery takes the money to Paris, and Whaley names violinist Louie Jones, Gulfport and Joe Stafford.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: And well we stayed over there and went all over Europe playing. We'd go to the officer's mess and we'd play and you'd get money and Vodrey used to take the money and go to Paris so one day the Lieutenant says we're going to Leone now which way shall we go. Shall we go through Paris or go the other way. We said, let's go to Paris, so he took us into Paris and when I got outside of Paris, I said so this is Paris bring on the women.

And we went into a place they had there, half of the place was for dancing and the other was for rollerskating and we played in the dance section and I remember we had a fellow in that band, Louie Jones. He was a great violin player from New York and he was from Boston, but he was a very great violinist.
Can you name any other guys that were in that band around that time. Remember any of the fellows' names.
Oh, gee, fellow named Gulfport, he was in the band. He was a comedian.
He used to play oompha. Horn.
And Stafford, Joe Stafford, he was trombone player. Oh, we had quite a few New York boys there, musicians and I can't remember them all.
Well, you just go on with your story.

Oh, yeah, we went to Paris and we played at the Ballroom and I remember a girl come up to Louie Jones and says, oh, you're beautiful and I said, see, I told you, Louie, you'd get all the gals and we left there --
You must have been a handsome dude in those days because you ain't bad now.
Who, me. Oh, I had plenty girls. The girl used to teach, I said, 'why don't you marry me' and she said 'no, if you come back here, then I'll marry you.'
I see from your complexion, you said your father was an Indian and I can see that sort of texture in your skin.
The redness is still here. I was telling Ruth about it --
